Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. @nsitharaman met Mr. Raj Ganguly, Co-founder and CEO of @BCapitalGroup, in Singapore today.

Discussions covered opportunities in Sovereign AI and the broader AI ecosystem. FM highlighted India’s potential to emerge as a leader in AI services and encouraged B Capital to explore the application of AI in banking and financial services in India. The B Capital team emphasised the importance of a stable currency and predictable, transparent tax policies for investors.

FM Smt. @nsitharaman also encouraged B Capital to explore investment opportunities through the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (@NIIFIndia) and GIFT IFSC, particularly those relating to pension funds.
The meeting was also attended by Mr. Karan Mohla, General Partner, B Capital.

results.text:
For capital markets models that are dependent upon share issuance ex: $MSTR | $ASST and all Digital Credit instruments, buybacks signal weakness to the market, not strength. 

Let's think it through: in the case of $STRC, the preferred exists to be issued above $100.01 so the proceeds can buy $BTC. If the company has to intervene in that market, they are essentially running the model in reverse. This isn't a judgment about the quality of $STRC as an instrument, but a statement about the buyback as a corporate action in this context. 

Now, I have been clear that there is a capital structure benefit to retiring shares, shrinking dividend obligations, etc. But that isn't "profit" or earnings that the company captures, nor are they a price lever. Furthermore, I think the market is treating the inorganic bid as support to sell into. 

None of these factors signal strength; strength for these $BTC meta-derivative equities is signaled via (a) share issuance (b) capital markets access and (c) consistent dividend payments. Right now, [2] out of the [3] signals are showing stress, so the market is testing both the resolve of the issuer and organic demand.
